info.description: Economics is the study of how society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into the subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While microeconomics focuses on the behavior of individual economic agents, this course - macroeconomics - studies how economists measure macroeconomic variables and covers topics such as determination of national output, economic growth, unemployment, inflation, interest rates, and exchange rates. Macroeconomics also discusses and assesses the effectiveness of monetary and fiscal policies under different scenarios.
info.studentTasks:
+ Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

+ Read textbooks and other materials in advance before the class

+ Actively participate in class activities

+ Complete all homework assignments and other tasks given by the instructor

+ Use personal laptop in class only for learning purposes

+ Don’t have private conversations or arrive at class late, which can disrupt the learning environment of the class

Recognize the influences of market equilibrium and disequilibrium

Review the influences of aggregate demand and aggregate supply
Shows self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context

assessments.questionType: Option 1: Students will be divided into 4-6 groups in the first session. Students could join some in-class activities as members of those groups. Each group will be assigned one topic, or will choose one topic subject to the instructor's approval, which is related to current economic issues in the real world. Students need to apply all comprehensive knowledge of macroeconomics to explain and analyze those issues. Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
